newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Moslems rebury kin in destroyed village.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Moslems rebury kin in destroyed village.

text.p: About 10,000 Moslems on Saturday reburied the bodies of 224 of their ethnic kin, who the Bosnian government alleges were massacred by Serb forces, in a sombre ceremony in the destroyed village of Biljani.

Rows of simple coffins covered with green flags bearing the Moslem crescent moon and star stood before empty graves as speakers recalled the morning of July 10, 1992 when residents of the village in northwestern Bosnia died.
The killings, which Moslems say included women and children, occurred in the opening months of the Bosnian war when Serb ethnic cleansing was at its height.

"They killed even children. They committed a crime against the Bosnian people, against the country of Bosnia and against European civilisation," said Bosnian Federation Vice-President Ejup Ganic. "We are asking for justice and we will never stop."
The bodies reburied on Saturday had been exhumed from two mass grave sites. Bosnian government authorities report that a total of 258 Moslems were killed in Biljani in the massacre.
